appellations.name: Tokaj
appellations.grapes: Furmint, Hárslevelű, Sárgamuskotály, Kövérszőlő, Zéta, Kabar
appellations.summary:
Tokaj is the one Hungarian appellation every wine lover knows, and one of the handful of sweet-wine regions in the world with genuine claim to greatness. It covers 27 settlements in the volcanic Zemplén foothills, from Abaújszántó and Monok in the west to Sátoraljaújhely in the north-east and Tokaj town at the confluence of the Bodrog and Tisza in the south. The official list in the current specification is: Abaújszántó, Bekecs, Bodrogkeresztúr, Bodrogkisfalud, Bodrogolaszi, Erdőbénye, Erdőhorváti, Golop, Hercegkút, Legyesbénye, Makkoshotyka, Mád, Mezőzombor, Monok, Olaszliszka, Rátka, Sárazsadány, Sárospatak, Sátoraljaújhely, Szegi, Szegilong, Szerencs, Tarcal, Tállya, Tokaj, Tolcsva and Vámosújfalu. (Ond, often listed separately, is now part of Szerencs.) Only vineyard land rated Class I or II in the cadastre counts.

What makes Tokaj special is the meeting of a late-ripening, high-acid grape (Furmint), a volcanic soil that gives the wine a smoky, saline grip, and a river microclimate that brings noble rot most autumns. The result is a family of wines unlike anything else: Eszencia, the near-unfermented nectar of aszú berries; Aszú, botrytised berries steeped in base wine, at least 120 g/l of sugar and 18 months in cask; Szamorodni, dry and nutty under flor or sweet; the rare Fordítás and Máslás; late harvest wines; and, since the 1990s, a fast-growing body of dry Furmint and Hárslevelű, often from named vineyards. Great Aszú tastes of apricot, orange peel, quince, honey, tea and walnut, with an acidity that keeps it fresh for a century.

The appellation is also one of the oldest legally protected wine regions in the world. Vineyards were ranked into classes between the 1720s and 1772, and a royal decree of 1737 limited the Tokaji name to defined towns and made new planting subject to permission. The landscape (cellars, villages, hills) has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2002.
appellations.terroir: Rhyolite, andesite and dacite with tuff layers, weathered to red *nyirok* clay or white kaolinitic soils; quartzite caps on some hills; loess on about 5% of the area (southern Tokaj hill around Tarcal and Tokaj). South-facing slopes of 120 to 300 m. Continental climate with long warm autumns; morning mists from the Bodrog and Tisza drive botrytis. Rock-cut cellars at 10 to 12 °C with walls furred in black cellar mould.
appellations.nerd_note: The modern 'puttonyos' label is only a hint: since 2013 every Aszú must have at least 120 g/l of sugar, '6 puttonyos' needs 150 g/l, and wines below 120 g/l can no longer be called Aszú at all. Old bottles labelled 3 or 4 puttonyos are pre-reform.

appellations.name: Eger
appellations.grapes: Kékfrankos, Kadarka, Pinot Noir, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Syrah; whites Leányka, Királyleányka, Olaszrizling, Hárslevelű, Furmint
appellations.summary:
Eger is the baroque town of castles, minarets and cellar valleys at the foot of the Bükk hills, and its wine district is Hungary's most famous red-wine name after Villány. Its emblem is Egri Bikavér ('Bull's Blood of Eger'), a blend of at least three (Classicus) or four (Superior) red varieties dominated by Kékfrankos, with Kadarka, Pinot Noir, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Syrah in support; no single grape may dominate too heavily. The name rests on the legend of the 1552 siege, when István Dobó's defenders supposedly frightened the Ottomans with red-stained beards. In Communist times Bikavér became a cheap export brand; today's good versions are spicy, medium-bodied, cherry-fruited and fresh rather than heavy.

Since 2010 Eger has built a white counterpart, Egri Csillag ('Star of Eger'), a blend led by aromatic varieties such as Leányka, Királyleányka, Olaszrizling, Hárslevelű and Furmint. Both blends follow a pyramid of Classicus, Superior and Grand Superior with stricter yields, mapped vineyards and longer ageing at the top. The district's 19 settlements include Eger, Andornaktálya, Demjén, Egerszalók, Felsőtárkány, Noszvaj and Ostoros; Pinot Noir from the Nagy-Eged hill is the region's other claim to fame.
appellations.terroir: Rhyolite tuff (soft enough to carve the Szépasszony-völgy cellars), andesite, clay and some limestone on south-facing foothills; cooler than southern Hungary, so later harvests and higher acidity.
appellations.nerd_note: Nagy-Eged hill above Eger reaches about 535 m with very steep south slopes; its Pinot Noir and Kékfrankos are among the most structured reds in northern Hungary.

appellations.name: Villány
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Portugieser, Kékfrankos, Kadarka, Pinot Noir; whites Olaszrizling, Hárslevelű, Chardonnay
appellations.summary:
Villány is Hungary's southernmost and warmest hill district, a 25 km strip along the southern face of the limestone Villány hills close to the Croatian border. Seventeen settlements belong to it, led by Villány, Villánykövesd, Palkonya, Nagyharsány and Siklós. After the Ottoman wars it was resettled by German 'Swabian' families, and their descendants (Bock, Gere, Tiffán, Polgár, Wunderlich, Heumann) built the cellar rows of Villány and Villánykövesd and led Hungary's first post-Communist quality revival. The district introduced Hungary's first origin-control system and the DHC (*Districtus Hungaricus Controllatus*) label term.

The wines are full-bodied, ripe reds. Portugieser (Kékoportó) was the old local grape for early-drinking wine; Bordeaux varieties took over after phylloxera and especially after 1990. Cabernet Franc proved the best fit, and in 2015 the growers created the Villányi Franc category, a premium Franc with strict yield, ageing and tasting rules. A quality pyramid of Classicus, Prémium and Villányi Franc, with single-vineyard wines from sites such as Kopár, Jammertal, Ördögárok and Konkoly, sits on top. Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Kékfrankos and Kadarka make up much of the rest, and Siklós, on the southern side, is known for whites.
appellations.terroir: Jurassic and Triassic limestone and dolomite under loess and red clay; sheltered south-facing slopes; sub-Mediterranean influence with hot summers and the highest sunshine hours in Hungary.
appellations.nerd_note: Zsigmond Teleki, born in Villány in 1854, established an experimental rootstock nursery there in 1881; his Berlandieri x Riparia seedlings were the source of rootstocks such as Kober 5BB and SO4, planted across Europe after phylloxera.

appellations.name: Szekszárd
appellations.grapes: Kadarka, Kékfrankos, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinot Noir; Olaszrizling, Chardonnay
appellations.summary:
Szekszárd sits on a block of deep loess hills above the Danube floodplain, about 150 km south of Budapest, with 15 settlements around the county town. The loess, in places tens of metres thick and cut into sunken lanes, gives the country's silkiest, most fragrant reds. The district's heritage grape is Kadarka, brought by Serbian settlers after the Ottoman era, which once made Szekszárd famous across the Habsburg lands. Phylloxera and Communist-era replanting replaced most of it with Kékfrankos and Bordeaux varieties, but growers such as Heimann and Takler have revived old Kadarka clones.

Szekszárdi Bikavér, a blend with a minimum share of Kadarka and led by Kékfrankos, is the district's answer to Eger and has strict local rules. Bordeaux blends, Merlot and Cabernet Franc can be excellent, and the loess makes softer, rounder versions than Villány's limestone. The district was home to the poet Mihály Babits and to some of Hungary's most respected family estates.
appellations.terroir: Thick Pleistocene loess over red clay (*vörösagyag*) and some limestone; deep sunken lanes (*löszmélyutak*); warm, sunny and fairly dry.
appellations.nerd_note: Heimann's Kadarka comes from a project that collected and replanted dozens of old Kadarka clones from local vineyards, rescuing the genetic diversity that commercial clones had lost.

appellations.name: Somlói
appellations.grapes: Juhfark, Olaszrizling, Furmint, Hárslevelű, Tramini
appellations.summary:
Somló is a single extinct volcano, a basalt butte rising 432 m out of the flat Kisalföld, and the smallest of Hungary's districts (about 300 to 400 ha in five settlements: Somlóvásárhely, Somlójenő, Somlószőlős, Doba and Borszörcsök). Its wines are among the most distinctive whites in Europe: dense, smoky, saline and austere in youth, built for years in bottle. The PDO allows only white grapes, led by Juhfark ('sheep's tail', after its long cylindrical bunches), Olaszrizling, Furmint, Hárslevelű and Tramini.

Somló's legend is that its wine guarantees a male heir. The Habsburg court is said to have served it on wedding nights, and the 'wedding night wine' story is still told at every cellar door. In the 19th century the Benedictine and Ursuline orders and noble families owned plots, and their small stone press houses still dot the slopes beneath the ruined castle. Today the hill is split among dozens of tiny growers; Kreinbacher's traditional-method sparkling wines are the most visible modern success.
appellations.terroir: Basalt cap and basalt tuff over Pannonian sand and clay; steep south and south-west slopes around a solitary hill that catches heat and wind on a flat plain.
appellations.nerd_note: Béla Fekete's Juhfark and Hárslevelű, aged in large old casks and released with years of age, showed how slowly the hill's wines evolve.

appellations.name: Nagy-Somló
appellations.grapes: Olaszrizling, Furmint, Hárslevelű, Chardonnay, Rajnai rizling, Szürkebarát and others
appellations.summary: Nagy-Somló ('Greater Somló') is the broader district PDO around Somló hill, adding five settlements to the five of Somló proper, including Celldömölk at the foot of the Ság hill and Kissomlyó. It permits a wider range of white varieties (Chardonnay, Rajnai rizling, Szürkebarát, Cserszegi fűszeres and others) and higher yields than the strict Somlói PDO, and it is used mainly for simpler whites from the volcanic satellites of the main hill.

appellations.name: Badacsony
appellations.grapes: Olaszrizling, Szürkebarát, Kéknyelű, Furmint, Rajnai rizling, Budai, Hárslevelű
appellations.summary: Badacsony is the district of the basalt 'witness hills' on the north-west shore of Lake Balaton: Badacsony itself (437 m), with its columnar basalt 'organ pipes', plus Szent György-hegy, Gulács, Tóti-hegy and Csobánc. Sixteen settlements share it. The lake reflects light and heat onto the slopes and the basalt and tuff soils give whites of real density and smoky minerality. Olaszrizling and Szürkebarát (Pinot Gris) dominate; Badacsony is also the last real home of Kéknyelű, an old variety with functionally female flowers that has to be interplanted with a pollinator such as Budai zöld, and which the Badacsony research station saved from near extinction.
appellations.terroir: Basalt caps, basalt tuff and Pannonian sand on steep south-facing slopes above the lake.
appellations.nerd_note: The poet Sándor Kisfaludy's 18th-century press house on Badacsony is now a restaurant; the 'Rózsakő' stone above it is the legendary meeting place of local lovers.

appellations.name: Balaton-felvidék
appellations.grapes: Olaszrizling, Szürkebarát, Cserszegi fűszeres, Rajnai rizling, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: The Balaton Uplands district stretches across the hills north and west of Lake Balaton, from Cserszegtomaj and Gyenesdiás near Keszthely to Sümeg and the Káli basin (23 settlements). It mixes volcanic, limestone and sandstone soils and makes mostly fresh dry whites: Olaszrizling, Szürkebarát, Rajnai rizling and the aromatic Cserszegi fűszeres, which was bred at nearby Keszthely and named after Cserszegtomaj.

appellations.name: Káli
appellations.grapes: Olaszrizling, Furmint, Kéknyelű, Juhfark, Szürkebarát, Kékfrankos and others
appellations.summary: The Káli basin is a small enclosed valley behind Badacsony, ringed by basalt hills and littered with sandstone 'stone seas' (*kőtenger*). Its PDO (2009) covers eight villages such as Köveskál, Kővágóörs, Szentbékkálla and Salföld and allows a long list of varieties. It has become a magnet for Budapest weekenders and small natural-leaning growers who make textured whites from Olaszrizling, Furmint and Kéknyelű.

appellations.name: Balatonfüred-Csopak
appellations.grapes: Olaszrizling, Rajnai rizling, Furmint, Chardonnay, Szürkebarát, Merlot, Cabernet
appellations.summary: This district lines the north-east shore of Lake Balaton from Balatonalmádi through Csopak and Balatonfüred to Zánka, 27 settlements in all, including the Tihany peninsula. Its signature is the red Permian sandstone and slate that colours the soil around Csopak, Paloznak and Lovas, which gives taut, salty Olaszrizling. Balatonfüred, the spa town where Hungary's first Anna Ball was held, adds limestone and marl. In recent years the growers have split off narrower PDOs (Csopak in 2020, Füred in 2025) to promote stricter, terroir-based wines.

appellations.name: Csopak
appellations.grapes: Olaszrizling, Furmint
appellations.summary: Csopak is a narrow PDO (2020) covering five villages on the north-east shore of Balaton (Csopak, Alsóörs, Felsőörs, Lovas, Paloznak) and only two grapes, Olaszrizling and Furmint, with a maximum of 9 t/ha. It grew out of the 'Csopak Codex', a voluntary charter signed by local growers in 2012 to raise Olaszrizling to a terroir wine. The red Permian sandstone and slate soils give firm, saline, almond-scented whites that age well, and producers such as Jásdi and Szent Donát label them by named vineyards.
appellations.nerd_note: Csopak's red earth is Permian sandstone, about 270 million years old, the same 'red bed' rock that colours the nearby village of Alsóörs.

appellations.name: Füred
appellations.grapes: Mainly white varieties (Olaszrizling and others)
appellations.summary: Füred is a new village-level PDO, listed in the EU register in November 2025, for wines from Balatonfüred and neighbouring communities on the north shore of Lake Balaton. The European Commission's summary describes dry, fresh wines of medium intensity with crisp acidity. Like Csopak before it, it sits inside the larger Balatonfüred-Csopak district and is meant to give the historic spa town's growers a tighter, more site-focused label.
appellations.nerd_note: Balatonfüred has held its Anna Ball every July since 1825, one of the oldest society balls in Hungary.

appellations.name: Tihany
appellations.grapes: Kékfrankos, Pinot Noir, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Zweigelt, Portugieser
appellations.summary: Tihany is a single-commune PDO on the volcanic peninsula that almost cuts Lake Balaton in two, crowned by the Benedictine abbey founded in 1055. Unusually for the north shore, the PDO is red-only: Kékfrankos, Pinot Noir, Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Zweigelt and Portugieser, at no more than 55 hl/ha. The peninsula's geyser cones, basalt tuff and warm microclimate ripen red grapes reliably, and the abbey's 11th-century charter is among the first documents to mention vineyards in Hungary.
appellations.nerd_note: The Tihany abbey's 1055 founding charter, written in Latin, contains the oldest surviving sentence fragment in Hungarian.

appellations.name: Balatonboglár
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Olaszrizling, Irsai Olivér, Muscat Ottonel, Pinot Noir, Kékfrankos, Merlot, Cabernet
appellations.summary: Balatonboglár covers the south shore of Lake Balaton and its hinterland (42 settlements in Somogy county). The soils are loess and sand, flatter and warmer than the north shore, and the wines are fruit-forward: aromatic whites, rosé, approachable reds and a great deal of sparkling wine, since the Balatonboglár winery (now Törley-owned) is a major sparkling producer. Ikon, Garamvári and Kristinus are among the estates.

appellations.name: Zala
appellations.grapes: Olaszrizling, Tramini, Rajnai rizling, Zöld veltelini, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: Zala is the westernmost Balaton district, spread over the hills of Zala county towards the Slovenian and Croatian borders (37 settlements). It is wetter and cooler than the lake shore, with loamy, sometimes sandy soils, and makes light whites (Olaszrizling, Tramini, Rajnai rizling, Zöld veltelini) plus sparkling base wine.

appellations.name: Balaton
appellations.grapes: Olaszrizling and a wide range of permitted varieties
appellations.summary: Balaton is the regional umbrella PDO covering the six Balaton districts (about 155 settlements). Producers use it to blend across districts or for simpler wines; the more specific district and village names carry the prestige.

appellations.name: Mátra
appellations.grapes: Olaszrizling, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Muscat Ottonel, Tramini, Zöld veltelini, Kékfrankos, Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Mátra is Hungary's second-largest hill district, on the southern foothills of the Mátra mountains (Hungary's highest, peaking at Kékes, 1,014 m) around Gyöngyös, Abasár, Gyöngyöspata and Domoszló (36 settlements). Andesite and andesite tuff give fresh, aromatic whites (Olaszrizling, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Muscat, Tramini, Zöld veltelini), and the cool slopes are increasingly used for Kékfrankos and Pinot Noir. Historically it fed Budapest's taverns; now growers such as Nagygombos, Szőke Mátyás and Benedek are building individual reputations.

appellations.name: Debrői Hárslevelű
appellations.grapes: Hárslevelű (plus permitted whites)
appellations.summary: Debrő, at the eastern foot of the Mátra around Aldebrő, Feldebrő and Verpelét, has been known for Hárslevelű for centuries, and the village name is fused with the grape in this PDO (2007). The wines are soft, perfumed and honeyed, often with a touch of sweetness. The Feldebrő church crypt, with 11th-century frescoes, is one of the oldest in Hungary.

appellations.name: Bükk
appellations.grapes: Olaszrizling, Leányka, Királyleányka, Chardonnay, Kékfrankos, Zweigelt
appellations.summary: Bükk is a small, cool district on the south-east slopes of the Bükk mountains near Miskolc, with 24 settlements including Bogács and Tibolddaróc, whose cellar villages are carved into rhyolite tuff. Olaszrizling, Leányka and Királyleányka make crisp whites; reds are light.

appellations.name: Sopron
appellations.grapes: Kékfrankos, Zweigelt, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Pinot Noir; Zöld veltelini, Tramini, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: Sopron, hugging the Austrian border on the south-west shore of Lake Fertő (Neusiedlersee), is Hungary's Kékfrankos country: about 60 percent of its vineyards are planted to it. It is the Hungarian continuation of Burgenland, and its wines (crunchy, spicy, sour-cherry reds) resemble those across the border. The town's Swabian growers (*poncichter*, from the German 'Bohnenzüchter', bean-growers, for the beans they grew between vine rows) kept the tradition alive. Franz Weninger's biodynamic estate at Balf and Ráspi in Fertőrákos are leading names; the district covers 18 settlements, extending south to Kőszeg's hills.
appellations.nerd_note: The Fertőrákos limestone quarry, worked since Roman times, is part of the Fertő/Neusiedlersee UNESCO landscape; the same Leitha limestone underlies some of Sopron's best Kékfrankos.

appellations.name: Kőszeg
appellations.grapes: Cool-climate whites and Kékfrankos (details in the 2025 specification)
appellations.summary: Kőszeg, a small walled town under the Alps' last foothills on the Austrian border, gained its own wine PDO in July 2025; the European Commission called it one of the oldest wine areas in Hungary. Its most famous custom is the *Szőlőjövés Könyve* (Book of the Coming of the Grapes): every year since 1740, on St George's Day (24 April), the length of the young vine shoots has been drawn into a town ledger, a unique 280-year phenological record.
appellations.nerd_note: The Book of the Coming of the Grapes is one of the longest continuous records of vine budbreak in Europe, now used by climate researchers.

appellations.name: Pannonhalma
appellations.grapes: Rajnai rizling, Olaszrizling, Sauvignon Blanc, Tramini, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Pannonhalma is the district below the Benedictine Archabbey of Pannonhalma, founded in 996 and a UNESCO site. The monks have made wine here for over a thousand years; the abbey's modern winery, rebuilt in 2003, makes precise whites (Rajnai rizling, Sauvignon Blanc, Tramini, Olaszrizling) and Pinot Noir from cool, windy slopes. Sixteen settlements around Győr belong to the district.

appellations.name: Mór
appellations.grapes: Ezerjó, Tramini, Rajnai rizling, Chardonnay, Leányka
appellations.summary: Mór, between the Vértes and Bakony hills, is the smallest Northern Pannonian district (six settlements) and the home of Ezerjó, a sharp, lean white once made both dry and as a botrytised sweet wine. Swabian settlers rebuilt the vineyards after the Ottoman wars; the 1956 'Ezerjó' tradition and a few dedicated growers keep the grape alive today.

appellations.name: Neszmély
appellations.grapes: Sauvignon Blanc, Irsai Olivér, Chardonnay, Olaszrizling, Cserszegi fűszeres
appellations.summary: Neszmély runs along the south bank of the Danube between Komárom and Esztergom (27 settlements). It is a cool, breezy white-wine district best known for the large modern Hilltop Neszmély winery, which pioneered clean, fruit-driven Hungarian whites for export in the 1990s. Sauvignon Blanc, Irsai Olivér, Chardonnay and Cserszegi fűszeres lead.

appellations.name: Etyek-Buda
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Olaszrizling, Zöld veltelini, Királyleányka, Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Etyek-Buda covers the limestone plateau west of Budapest (Etyek, Bicske, Velence) plus the Buda hills and the capital's Budafok district. Its product specification describes lime-rich brown forest soils on limestone, average temperatures of 9.5 to 10.5 °C and constant north-westerly winds: ideal for crisp whites and sparkling base wine. József Törley founded his champagne-method house at Budafok in 1882, and by the early 1910s the area made about two million bottles a year. Today Etyek is Budapest's weekend wine village, with Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Noir and Királyleányka from producers such as Etyeki Kúria, Haraszthy and Nyakas.

appellations.name: Etyeki pezsgő
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and other permitted varieties
appellations.summary: Etyeki pezsgő is a sparkling-wine PDO approved by the European Commission in November 2025 for bottle-aged sparkling wine from the Etyek area. The Commission's summary cites limestone bedrock, constant wind and cool, humid air, which give fresh, citrus-fruited wines with firm acidity, and notes that older bottles develop biscuit and bread-crust notes. It formalises Etyek's long role as the vineyard of Budapest's sparkling-wine houses.

appellations.name: Pécs
appellations.grapes: Cirfandli, Olaszrizling, Chardonnay, Kékfrankos, Cabernet, Merlot
appellations.summary: Pécs spreads over the warm southern slopes of the Mecsek hills around the city of Pécs, Roman Sopianae, and south to Mohács (33 settlements). It is the home of Cirfandli (Zierfandler), a spicy, late-ripening white that the local growers have taken as their emblem, and of the 19th-century Littke sparkling wine house.

appellations.name: Tolna
appellations.grapes: Olaszrizling, Chardonnay, Kékfrankos, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
appellations.summary: Tolna is a large, varied district between Szekszárd and Lake Balaton (54 settlements) with loess and sandy soils. It produces everyday whites, rosé and reds, and its Dunaföldvár and Bölcske corners on the Danube make some good Kékfrankos and Chardonnay.

appellations.name: Pannon
appellations.grapes: Wide range of permitted varieties
appellations.summary: Pannon is the umbrella PDO for the four southern Transdanubian districts (Villány, Szekszárd, Pécs and Tolna), about 120 settlements, used for cross-district blends and simpler wines. It lets a producer blend Szekszárd Kékfrankos with Villány Cabernet, for instance, and still sell a protected-origin wine; the district names carry the prestige.

appellations.name: Kunság
appellations.grapes: Olaszrizling, Ezerjó, Kövidinka, Cserszegi fűszeres, Arany sárfehér, Kékfrankos, Kadarka
appellations.summary: Kunság is Hungary's largest wine district, more than 100 settlements on the sandy plain between the Danube and Tisza around Kecskemét, Kiskőrös and Cegléd. The vineyards were planted on loose sand from the 1880s precisely because phylloxera cannot live in it, and the sand still makes ungrafted vines possible. Most of the output is light, inexpensive wine and sparkling base, but a few producers make lively whites from Ezerjó, Kövidinka, Cserszegi fűszeres and Olaszrizling and fresh Kadarka and Kékfrankos.
appellations.nerd_note: The Miklóstelep demonstration vineyard near Kecskemét, planted on land the town gave the state in 1883, proved that vines could be grown phylloxera-free on sand.

appellations.name: Izsáki Arany Sárfehér
appellations.grapes: Arany Sárfehér
appellations.summary: A single-variety PDO (2007) for Arany Sárfehér ('golden yellow-white'), a high-acid, neutral old grape grown on the sands around Izsák in the Kunság. Its sharp acidity made it a good base for sparkling wine, and that is still its main use. Ten settlements are covered.

appellations.name: Soltvadkerti
appellations.grapes: Ezerjó
appellations.summary: Soltvadkerti (2020) is a one-commune PDO for Ezerjó from Soltvadkert on the Kunság sands, a town that once had one of the densest concentrations of vineyards on the Great Plain. The rules allow only Ezerjó, making a crisp, citrusy white.

appellations.name: Monor
appellations.grapes: Ezerjó, Olaszrizling, Kövidinka, Kékfrankos, Kadarka and others
appellations.summary: Monor (2018) is a small PDO for four settlements south-east of Budapest (Monor, Monorierdő, Bénye, Gomba), centred on the Monor cellar hill (Strázsahegy), which holds about 900 small cellars, one of the largest cellar villages in Hungary.

appellations.name: Csongrád
appellations.grapes: Kadarka, Kékfrankos, Olaszrizling, Cserszegi fűszeres
appellations.summary: Csongrád lies east of the Kunság on the sandy plains near Szeged and Csongrád along the Tisza (19 settlements). It is one of the warmest and driest parts of Hungary, producing mostly Kadarka, Kékfrankos and simple whites; its Kadarka has a small revival following.

appellations.name: Hajós-Baja
appellations.grapes: Kékfrankos, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Zweigelt, Olaszrizling
appellations.summary: Hajós-Baja is the southern Great Plain district on the left bank of the Danube (17 settlements), on loess-covered sand that is a little richer than the Kunság's. It is famous for the cellar village (*pincefalu*) of Hajós, more than 1,200 cellars and press houses built by Swabian settlers on their own streets outside the village. Reds lead: Kékfrankos, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and Zweigelt.

appellations.name: Duna
appellations.grapes: Wide range of permitted varieties
appellations.summary: Duna is the umbrella PDO for the three Great Plain districts (Kunság, Csongrád, Hajós-Baja), about 150 settlements, for cross-district wines. It is mostly used for fresh, inexpensive whites, rosé and light reds from the sandy plains, often sold in bulk or under brand names.

appellations.name: Goriška Brda
appellations.grapes: Rebula, Zeleni sauvignon (Friulano), Malvazija, Chardonnay, Sivi pinot, Sauvignon, Pikolit; Merlot, Cabernet, Pokalca
appellations.summary: Goriška Brda ('Gorizia hills') is the Slovenian half of the Collio, a maze of flysch ridges and hilltop villages between the Soča and Idrija rivers on the Italian border, about 1,800 ha. Its signature grape is Rebula (Ribolla Gialla), which makes everything from crisp, citrusy whites to amber wines macerated for months on the skins. Zeleni sauvignon (Friulano), Malvazija, Chardonnay, Sivi pinot and the sweet Pikolit add range; Merlot and Cabernet thrive on the warmer slopes, and the local red Pokalca (Schioppettino) persists. The cooperative Klet Brda in Dobrovo is Slovenia's largest producer, but the district's name abroad comes from family estates: Movia, Klinec, Kabaj, Edi Simčič, Marjan Simčič, Ščurek, Erzetič, Dolfo, Štekar and Gašper.
appellations.terroir: Eocene flysch (*opoka*): alternating marl and sandstone that weathers into well-drained, lime-rich soil; terraced slopes of 75 to 400 m; the Julian Alps block cold northern air and the Adriatic is 25 km away.
appellations.nerd_note: Movia's Puro sparkling wine is sold undisgorged; the drinker opens it upside down under water (or into a bowl) to release the lees, a theatrical ritual devised by Aleš Kristančič.

appellations.name: Vipavska dolina
appellations.grapes: Zelen, Pinela, Rebula, Malvazija, Laški rizling, Sauvignon, Chardonnay; Merlot, Barbera, Refošk
appellations.summary: The Vipava valley runs west from the Nanos plateau towards Gorizia, a corridor where the bora wind blows hard enough to tip lorries; growers build stone walls and plant trees as windbreaks. About 2,100 ha on flysch slopes make fresh and macerated whites from Rebula, Malvazija, Laški rizling, Sauvignon and the two natives, Zelen (herbal, gooseberry-like) and Pinela (light and nervy), plus reds from Merlot, Barbera and Refošk. Batič, Mlečnik, Guerila, Burja, Sutor, Tilia and Lepa Vida are among the leading estates.
appellations.terroir: Flysch and marl on the valley sides, alluvium on the floor; sub-Mediterranean climate swept by the bora, which keeps vines dry and healthy.
appellations.nerd_note: Zelen and Pinela were nearly extinct in the 1980s; Vipava growers rebuilt them from a few old vineyards, and both are now protected local specialities.

appellations.name: Kras
appellations.grapes: Refošk (Teran), Vitovska, Malvazija, Sauvignon, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: The Kras (Karst) is the limestone plateau behind Trieste, about 560 ha of vineyard in pockets of red earth between dolines, dry-stone walls and sumac. It is the home of Teran, the deep purple, high-acid wine of Refošk grown on terra rossa, and of Vitovska and Malvazija whites, often macerated. Families such as Čotar, Renčel, Lisjak and Štoka in villages like Tomaj, Dutovlje and Gorjansko age their wines in caves cut into the limestone.
appellations.terroir: Iron-rich terra rossa in hollows of karst limestone, 200 to 400 m; thin soils, drought stress and the bora.
appellations.nerd_note: Kras growers often have to break the limestone with machines and import soil to plant a vineyard, which is why the district stays tiny.

appellations.name: Teran
appellations.grapes: Refošk (100%)
appellations.summary: Teran is a recognised traditional designation (PTP) and EU PDO for red wine made 100% from Refošk on the terra rossa of the Kras. The iron-rich soil gives a deep purple wine with very high acidity, sour cherry and blackberry fruit and a reputation in local folk medicine for being good for the blood. Traditionally it is drunk young with Karst prosciutto (*pršut*). Croatian Istria also uses the name Teran for a related but distinct grape; a 2017 EU derogation allowing Croatian producers to put Teran on labels alongside 'Hrvatska Istra' was contested by Slovenia in the EU courts.
appellations.terroir: Terra rossa over limestone on the Karst plateau.
appellations.nerd_note: Teran's maximum yield (90 hl/ha) is higher than other Slovenian PDOs because Refošk on the Karst crops modestly anyway; its high natural acidity is the defining analytical trait.

appellations.name: Slovenska Istra
appellations.grapes: Malvazija, Refošk, Rumeni muškat, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
appellations.summary: Slovenska Istra covers the warm flysch hills behind the Slovenian coast at Koper, Izola and Piran, about 1,850 ha. Malvazija is the white and Refošk the red, along with Cabernet, Merlot and the local Muškat. The large Vinakoper cooperative and family wineries such as Santomas, Rojac, Korenika & Moškon and Pucer z Vrha make most of the wine.

appellations.name: Štajerska Slovenija
appellations.grapes: Laški rizling, Šipon, Sauvignon, Renski rizling, Sivi pinot, Traminec, Muškat, Kerner, Ranina
appellations.summary: Štajerska Slovenija is the largest Slovenian district, about 5,400 ha across the steep hills of Slovenian Styria from Maribor and Ptuj to Ljutomer-Ormož, Haloze and Slovenske gorice. It shares its style with Austria's Südsteiermark across the border: racy, aromatic whites from Sauvignon Blanc, Laški rizling, Šipon (Furmint), Renski rizling, Sivi pinot, Traminec, Muškat and Kerner, often grown on terraces at 30 degrees or more, plus late-harvest, botrytis and ice wines. Jeruzalem in Ljutomer-Ormož and the Haloze hills near Ptuj are the classic sites; producers include Puklavec, Verus, Steyer, Gaube, Kogl, Valdhuber, Heaps Good Wine and the old cooperatives Ptujska klet and Vinag.
appellations.terroir: Marl, sandstone and clay on steep terraced hills; continental climate with long, cool autumns.
appellations.nerd_note: Dveri-Pax is the wine estate of Admont Abbey in Austria, whose Benedictines held vineyards near Jarenina from the 12th century.

appellations.name: Prekmurje
appellations.grapes: Laški rizling, Šipon, Sauvignon, Renski rizling, Beli pinot
appellations.summary: Prekmurje is the flat-to-rolling Pannonian corner of Slovenia beyond the Mura, bordering Hungary and Austria, with about 440 ha in two hill groups: the Goričko hills and the Lendavske gorice. The wines are Laški rizling, Šipon, Sauvignon and Renski rizling, and the area has a strong Hungarian minority; Marof's Mačkovci winery has given the district international attention.

appellations.name: Dolenjska
appellations.grapes: Žametovka, Modra frankinja, Kraljevina, Laški rizling, Rumeni plavec
appellations.summary: Dolenjska is the hilly heart of Posavje around Novo mesto and Trebnje, about 1,350 ha of small vineyards and *zidanice* cottages. It is best known for Cviček but also makes varietal Modra frankinja, Žametovka and whites from Kraljevina, Laški rizling and Rumeni plavec.

appellations.name: Cviček
appellations.grapes: Žametovka, Modra frankinja, Kraljevina, Laški rizling, Rumeni plavec
appellations.summary: Cviček is a recognised traditional designation for a light, pale red wine from Dolenjska made by blending red and white grapes: mainly Žametovka and Modra frankinja with Kraljevina, Laški rizling and others. It is low in alcohol (typically 8.5 to 10%) and high in acidity, drunk young and cool. Slovenia's ministry approved an amended specification for Cviček in September 2025.
appellations.nerd_note: Cviček is one of the few protected wines in the EU that must blend red and white grapes; its low alcohol made it a 'doctor's wine' recommended to convalescents.

appellations.name: Bizeljsko Sremič
appellations.grapes: Laški rizling, Rumeni plavec, Ranfol, Kraljevina, Modra frankinja, Žametovka
appellations.summary: Bizeljsko Sremič lies in the far east of Posavje by the Croatian border, about 700 ha. Quartz sand under the vineyards let growers dig *repnice*, caves originally for storing turnips (*repa*) that now age wine at a steady temperature. The district makes Bizeljčan blends, sweet wines and traditional-method sparkling (Istenič is the best-known house).

appellations.name: Bizeljčan
appellations.grapes: White: Laški rizling, Rumeni plavec, Ranfol; red: Modra frankinja, Žametovka, Portugalka
appellations.summary: Bizeljčan is the recognised traditional designation of Bizeljsko Sremič, made as a white blend (Laški rizling, Rumeni plavec, Ranfol, Kraljevina and others) and as a red (Modra frankinja, Žametovka, Portugalka). Both are light, fresh, everyday wines.

appellations.name: Bela krajina
appellations.grapes: Modra frankinja, Žametovka, Laški rizling, Kraljevina, Rumeni muškat
appellations.summary: Bela krajina ('White March'), named for its birch trees and white linen dress, is a small district (about 300 ha) on the Kolpa river by the Croatian border around Metlika, Semič and Črnomelj. It makes Metliška črnina, Belokranjec, Modra frankinja and some of Slovenia's best ice wines and botrytised sweet wines.

appellations.name: Metliška črnina
appellations.grapes: Modra frankinja, Žametovka, Portugalka, Šentlovrenka, Gamay, Modri pinot, Zweigelt
appellations.summary: Metliška črnina ('black of Metlika') is Bela krajina's traditional red blend, dominated by Modra frankinja and Žametovka with Portugalka, Šentlovrenka, Gamay and others. It is deep coloured, dry, medium-bodied and fruity. The ministry approved an amended specification in March 2026.

appellations.name: Belokranjec
appellations.grapes: Laški rizling, Kraljevina, Beli pinot, Chardonnay, Rumeni muškat, Zeleni silvanec, Renski rizling
appellations.summary: Belokranjec is the white partner of Metliška črnina: a fresh, fragrant white blend from Bela krajina based on Laški rizling, Kraljevina, Beli pinot, Rumeni muškat and Zeleni silvanec. Its amended specification was approved in March 2026.

appellations.name: Dingač
appellations.grapes: Plavac Mali
appellations.summary: Dingač is Croatia's most famous red wine and its first protected wine region (1961): a steep strip of south-west-facing slopes on the Pelješac peninsula above the sea, between Trstenik and Borak, worked from the village of Potomje on the other side of the ridge. Only Plavac Mali is permitted, with a maximum of 8 t/ha. The slopes reach 45 degrees on crumbling dolomitic limestone with almost no topsoil, and the vines get sun from above, light reflected from the sea and heat radiated by the stones, so the grapes shrivel and concentrate. The wines are dark, tannic, often 15% alcohol or more, with dried fig, carob, black cherry, tobacco and herb notes. Until 1975 the grapes went over the ridge by donkey; the growers' cooperative then financed a 400 m tunnel from Potomje. The protected area covers about 758 ha, of which about 78 ha are planted.
appellations.terroir: Karst dolomite and limestone scree, slopes up to 45 degrees, 0 to 300 m above the sea, extreme sun and heat; dry-farmed bush vines.
appellations.nerd_note: Plavac Mali is a cross of Tribidrag (Zinfandel) and Dobričić, an old variety from the island of Šolta, so every bottle of Dingač is Zinfandel's grandchild in a sense.

appellations.name: Ponikve
appellations.grapes: Plavac Mali, Pošip, Maraština
appellations.summary: Ponikve, registered in February 2021 as Croatia's 17th wine PDO, is a small plateau and hamlet near Ston at the neck of the Pelješac peninsula. The PDO covers wines from Plavac Mali, Pošip and Maraština, including a style made from raisined grapes, and was created to give the locality's name visibility on labels. Ponikve's karst fields sit higher and cooler than the south-facing Dingač slopes.

appellations.name: Muškat momjanski
appellations.grapes: Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains (Momjan muscat)
appellations.summary: Muškat momjanski is a PDO (August 2021) for wines from Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains grown around the hilltop village of Momjan near Buje in north-west Istria. Momjan's muscat was famous in the Habsburg period; today it is made dry, off-dry and as a sweet late-harvest wine with orange-blossom and honey notes. Kozlović and Prelac are among the producers.

appellations.name: Hrvatska Istra
appellations.grapes: Malvazija Istarska, Teran, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Refošk, Muscat
appellations.summary: Hrvatska Istra is the subregional PDO for Croatian Istria, 41 municipalities from Umag and Buje to Pula and Labin. It is Croatia's most dynamic wine region: Malvazija Istarska makes up about half the plantings, followed by Teran, Merlot, Cabernet, Refošk and Muscat. The west coast's red terra rossa gives riper, rounder wines; the grey and white marls of the interior around Motovun, Buje and Momjan give tighter whites. Producers range from the large Agrolaguna to family estates such as Kozlović, Matošević, Roxanich, Clai, Coronica, Trapan, Kabola, Benvenuti, Cattunar and Arman.
appellations.nerd_note: Croatian producers can label Teran only with 'Hrvatska Istra' alongside it, under a 2017 EU derogation that Slovenia, which holds the Teran PDO, contested.

appellations.name: Hrvatsko primorje
appellations.grapes: Žlahtina, Gegić, Sansigot, Trojišćina, Malvazija
appellations.summary: Hrvatsko primorje covers the Kvarner gulf and its islands (Krk, Cres, Lošinj, Rab, Pag) and the coast from Rijeka to Karlobag. Its best-known wine is Vrbnička Žlahtina from Vrbnik on Krk, a light, fresh, floral white from the native Žlahtina; Pag's Gegić is another island specialty.

appellations.name: Sjeverna Dalmacija
appellations.grapes: Babić, Plavac Mali, Lasina, Debit, Maraština
appellations.summary: Northern Dalmatia runs from Zadar to Primošten and Rogoznica, with the islands of Pašman, Ugljan and the Kornati. Its signature is Babić, a dark, firm red grown around Primošten and Šibenik in tiny vineyards hacked out of bare limestone and protected by dry-stone walls; Debit and Maraština are the whites.

appellations.name: Srednja i Južna Dalmacija
appellations.grapes: Plavac Mali, Tribidrag, Pošip, Grk, Bogdanuša, Vugava, Malvasija Dubrovačka, Maraština
appellations.summary: Central and Southern Dalmatia covers the coast from Trogir and Split to Dubrovnik and Konavle plus the islands of Brač, Hvar, Vis, Korčula, Šolta, Lastovo and Mljet, and Pelješac. It holds most of Croatia's great coastal wines: Plavac Mali from Pelješac (Postup, Trstenik), Hvar (Sveta Nedjelja, Ivan Dolac) and Brač; Pošip and Grk from Korčula; Bogdanuša from Hvar; Vugava from Vis; Crljenak Kaštelanski from Kaštela; and Malvasija Dubrovačka from Konavle.

appellations.name: Dalmatinska zagora
appellations.grapes: Kujundžuša, Trnjak, Debit, Maraština, Plavac Mali
appellations.summary: Dalmatinska zagora is the karst hinterland behind the coast, from Knin and Drniš to Sinj, Imotski and Vrgorac. Its higher, drier and cooler plateaus give fresher wines than the coast; Kujundžuša (Imotski) and Trnjak are the local grapes, and Debit grows around Drniš.

appellations.name: Primorska Hrvatska
appellations.grapes: All permitted coastal varieties
appellations.summary: Primorska Hrvatska is the regional umbrella PDO for all of coastal Croatia (Istria, Kvarner and Dalmatia), about 180 municipalities, used for wines blended across subregions. A producer who buys Plavac Mali from Pelješac and Babić from Primošten for one wine, for instance, labels it Primorska Hrvatska; most quality wines name their subregion instead.

appellations.name: Slavonija
appellations.grapes: Graševina, Traminac, Chardonnay, Pinot Blanc, Sauvignon, Frankovka
appellations.summary: Slavonija is the subregion of the hills ringing the Požega basin and the northern slopes toward the Drava: Kutjevo, Orahovica, Feričanci, Đakovo, Slavonski Brod, Daruvar and Pakrac. Its 'Golden Valley' around Kutjevo is Croatia's Graševina heartland, with wines from crisp and appley to oak-aged and botrytised; Traminac, Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Sauvignon and Frankovka also do well. Cistercians built Kutjevo's first cellar in 1232.
appellations.terroir: Loess, clay and marl on south-facing slopes of the Papuk and Krndija hills at 150 to 350 m; continental climate.

appellations.name: Hrvatsko Podunavlje
appellations.grapes: Graševina, Traminac, Rhine Riesling, Chardonnay, Frankovka, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: Croatian Danube covers the loess ridges along the Danube in Baranja (Zmajevac, Kneževi Vinogradi), Erdut and Srijem (Ilok). Ilok's Traminac and Graševina, from the large Iločki podrumi, are the best-known wines; Erdutski vinogradi and Belje are other major estates.

appellations.name: Istočna kontinentalna Hrvatska
appellations.grapes: Graševina and other permitted continental varieties
appellations.summary: The regional umbrella PDO for eastern continental Croatia, covering Slavonija and Hrvatsko Podunavlje (133 municipalities), used for wines blended across the two subregions, typically larger-volume Graševina from producers who buy fruit from both Slavonia and the Danube.

appellations.name: Plešivica
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Graševina, Rhine Riesling, Sauvignon, Portugizac
appellations.summary: Plešivica, a low range of hills west of Zagreb around Jastrebarsko and Samobor, is Croatia's sparkling-wine capital and one of its most forward-thinking areas. Tomac, Korak, Režek, Jagunić and Šember make traditional-method sparkling and still wines from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Riesling, Graševina, Sauvignon and Portugizac; Tomac also ferments in buried amphorae.

appellations.name: Zagorje – Međimurje
appellations.grapes: Pušipel (Furmint), Sauvignon, Rhine Riesling, Graševina, Traminac, Muscat
appellations.summary: Zagorje-Međimurje covers the hills of Hrvatsko Zagorje north of Zagreb and Međimurje between the Mura and Drava, against the Slovenian and Hungarian borders. Međimurje's steep Štrigova hills make taut, aromatic Sauvignon, Riesling and Pušipel (local Furmint), and some excellent late-harvest wines.

appellations.name: Prigorje-Bilogora
appellations.grapes: Kraljevina, Graševina, Pinot Gris, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Prigorje-Bilogora takes in the slopes north and east of Zagreb (Zelina, Križevci, Koprivnica, Bjelovar). It makes light whites, notably Kraljevina around Sveti Ivan Zelina, plus Graševina and Pinot Gris. Zelina's Kraljevina, a pink-skinned, low-alcohol local grape, is the classic wine of Zagreb's taverns.

appellations.name: Moslavina
appellations.grapes: Škrlet, Graševina, Chardonnay, Sauvignon
appellations.summary: Moslavina is a small hill range south-east of Zagreb around Kutina and Popovača. It is the home of Škrlet, a native white with light body, citrus and herbal notes, rescued from near-extinction and now the subregion's calling card.

appellations.name: Pokuplje
appellations.grapes: Graševina, Kraljevina, Chardonnay, Portugizac
appellations.summary: Pokuplje follows the Kupa river south-west of Zagreb around Karlovac and Ozalj; a small, cool subregion of light whites (Graševina, Kraljevina, Chardonnay) and some Portugizac. Its scattered hillside plots are mostly family vineyards for home consumption, with only a few commercial bottlers.

appellations.name: Zapadna kontinentalna Hrvatska
appellations.grapes: All permitted continental varieties
appellations.summary: The regional umbrella PDO for western continental Croatia, covering the five upland subregions (about 200 municipalities): Plešivica, Zagorje-Međimurje, Prigorje-Bilogora, Moslavina and Pokuplje. It is used for wines that blend fruit across those hills or do not qualify for a subregion name.

appellations.name: Fruška Gora
appellations.grapes: Graševina, Riesling, Sremska Zelenika, Morava, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Frankovka, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: Fruška Gora is a forested ridge on the right bank of the Danube opposite Novi Sad, rising to 539 m, with vineyards on its loess and marl slopes. Probus is credited with planting it in the 3rd century, and from the 16th century its sixteen Orthodox monasteries kept the vine alive. Sremski Karlovci, the old metropolitan seat at its eastern foot, is the wine capital and the home of Bermet. Today about 60 wineries work the ridge, making Graševina, Riesling, Sremska Zelenika, Morava, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc and reds from Frankovka, Merlot and Cabernet. Leading names include Kovačević, Erdevik (whose cellar dates to 1826), Trivanović, Probus, Šijački and Živanović.
appellations.terroir: Loess and marl over Paleozoic schist; south-facing slopes 150 to 400 m; continental climate tempered by the Danube.

appellations.name: Srem
appellations.grapes: Graševina, Riesling, Chardonnay, Frankovka, Merlot
appellations.summary: Srem is the broader PGI for the Syrmia region between the Danube and the Sava, including Fruška Gora and its plains. It is used for blends and for wines from the lower slopes.

appellations.name: Vršac
appellations.grapes: Graševina, Banat Riesling, Rhine Riesling, Kreaca, Chardonnay, Smederevka, Frankovka
appellations.summary: Vršac lies at the foot of the Vršac hills, the only real elevation of the Serbian Banat, near the Romanian border. In the 19th century its vineyards spread over about 10,000 ha; today about 2,000 ha remain, much of it once worked by the state company Vršački vinogradi, whose 1968 'New Cellar' with a capacity of about 20 million litres was one of the largest in Europe. Riesling (Italian, Banat and Rhine), Kreaca, Chardonnay and Frankovka grow on loess and schist; Gudurica's estates (Vinarija Selecta, Kreačić) and Vršac's family wineries are reviving quality.

appellations.name: Banat
appellations.grapes: Graševina, Riesling, Kreaca, Smederevka, Frankovka
appellations.summary: Banat is the broad PGI for the Serbian part of the historic Banat region east of the Tisa, divided further into Southern Banat, Northern Banat and Banat-Tisa. It is mostly flat, with vineyards concentrated around Vršac and Bela Crkva.

appellations.name: Southern Banat
appellations.grapes: Graševina, Riesling, Kreaca, Frankovka, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: Southern Banat covers the Vršac hills, Bela Crkva and the Deliblato sands down to the Danube; it is the most important part of the Serbian Banat for wine. Riesling, Kreaca and Frankovka from the Vršac hills are its best-known wines.

appellations.name: Palić
appellations.grapes: Riesling, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Muscat, Kadarka, Frankovka, Cabernet Franc
appellations.summary: Palić, a resort lake near Subotica on the Hungarian border, grows vines on wind-blown sands that once kept phylloxera at bay. Zvonko Bogdan, the famous tamburica singer, built a 62 ha estate here; Vinarija Čoka and Dibonis are other producers.

appellations.name: Subotica-Horgoš Sands
appellations.grapes: Kadarka, Graševina, Riesling, Kövidinka
appellations.summary: The Subotica-Horgoš sands in the far north are a continuation of Hungary's Great Plain sand vineyards, planted on dunes that phylloxera could not penetrate. Light whites and Kadarka are traditional.

appellations.name: Deliblato Sands
appellations.grapes: Graševina, Smederevka, Kreaca, Frankovka
appellations.summary: Deliblato Sands, Europe's largest continental sand area, in the southern Banat, has vineyards on its edges planted, like Hungary's Kunság, on phylloxera-proof sand. The dunes, now a nature reserve, were stabilised with forest in the 19th century, and the vineyards on their fringes make light, fresh whites.

appellations.name: Oplenac
appellations.grapes: Traminer, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Tamjanika, Pinot Noir, Gamay, Prokupac, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: Oplenac is the hill above Topola where King Peter I built the white marble Church of St George and the Karađorđević mausoleum. His son, King Alexander I, built the King's Winery at its foot in 1931 on the French model, with two underground floors held at 8 °C and 99 oak casks of 2,000 litres, and planted over 50 ha with Traminer, Chardonnay, Gamay and Pinot Noir. The vineyards were neglected after 1945 and replanted in the 2000s; the first new harvest was in 2006. Aleksandrović's Trijumf, a nearby estate wine, follows a royal blend recipe from 1932.

appellations.name: Šumadija-Velika Morava
appellations.grapes: Smederevka, Tamjanika, Prokupac, Chardonnay, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: Šumadija-Velika Morava is the broad PGI for the central Serbian heartland between the Sava, Danube and Velika Morava, around Topola, Kragujevac, Aranđelovac, Smederevo and Jagodina. It is the catch-all name for wines blended across the rolling, mixed-farming hills of the Serbian heartland.

appellations.name: Župa
appellations.grapes: Prokupac, Tamjanika, Smederevka, Graševina, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
appellations.summary: Župa is a warm, sheltered valley around Aleksandrovac in the Rasina district, ringed by the Kopaonik, Goč and Jastrebac mountains, and Serbia's self-styled wine capital. Monastic charters record its vineyards in the Nemanjić era, and legend says Prince Lazar's army took communion with Župa wine before the 1389 Battle of Kosovo. Prokupac and Tamjanika are the stars. Aleksandrovac's Župska berba harvest festival has run every September since 1963, and the town has a museum of viticulture.

appellations.name: Kruševac
appellations.grapes: Prokupac, Tamjanika, Smederevka, Vranac
appellations.summary: Kruševac, Prince Lazar's medieval capital, is home to the Rubin company, once Yugoslavia's largest brandy and wine producer. The PGI covers the surrounding Rasina hills, which share the warm, sheltered conditions of neighbouring Župa and grow Prokupac and Tamjanika.

appellations.name: Levač
appellations.grapes: Prokupac, Tamjanika, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
appellations.summary: Levač is a hilly district west of the Velika Morava near Rekovac, home to Lastar (founded 2013) and other new wineries reviving Prokupac and Tamjanika on the district's rolling clay hills.

appellations.name: Belgrade
appellations.grapes: Smederevka, Graševina, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
appellations.summary: The Belgrade PGI covers vineyards within the capital's territory, including Grocka on the Danube and the Kosmaj and Dubona hills to the south. Grocka's Danube slopes were among the capital's main vineyards before the city spread.

appellations.name: Negotin
appellations.grapes: Prokupac, Gamay, Crna Tamjanika, Bagrina, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
appellations.summary: Negotin, in the Krajina by the Danube's Iron Gates near the Bulgarian and Romanian borders, is famous for its stone cellar villages (*pivnice*) at Rajac, Rogljevo and Štubik, on Serbia's UNESCO Tentative List since 2010. Its warm hills grow Prokupac, black Tamjanika, Gamay, Bagrina and Bordeaux varieties. During France's phylloxera crisis Negotin wine was sold to French merchants.

appellations.name: Rajac
appellations.grapes: Prokupac, Gamay, Tamjanika, Bagrina
appellations.summary: Rajac is a village in the Negotin Krajina whose cellar settlement, about 2 km west on the Beli Breg hill, is the finest of the region's pivnice: a cluster of stone cellars with arched portals along winding lanes next to a 19th-century cemetery. The PGI covers its vineyards.

appellations.name: Krajina
appellations.grapes: Prokupac, Gamay, Tamjanika, Bagrina
appellations.summary: Krajina is the PGI for the wider Negotin Krajina along the Danube and Timok, framing Negotin, Rajac, Mihajlovac and Ključ. The Danube's Iron Gates gorge moderates the climate, and the area's stone cellar villages are unique in the Balkans.

appellations.name: Timok
appellations.grapes: Prokupac, Gamay, Tamjanika, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
appellations.summary: Timok is the broad PGI for the Timok river valley in eastern Serbia, from Knjaževac through Zaječar to Negotin. Small family wineries around Knjaževac and Zaječar are reviving the area, and the late-Roman palace of Felix Romuliana near Zaječar is a reminder of the valley's ancient importance.

appellations.name: Toplica
appellations.grapes: Prokupac, Tamjanika, Smederevka, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: Toplica, the valley of the Toplica river around Prokuplje, gave its name to Prokupac and remains the grape's heartland. Warm summers give fuller, spicier Prokupac than in the north, and growers here are leading the effort to make the grape a serious varietal wine rather than a blending component.

appellations.name: Prokuplje
appellations.grapes: Prokupac, Tamjanika
appellations.summary: Prokuplje, the medieval town that gave Prokupac its name, has its own PGI for the hills around the town in the Toplica valley. The town's name and the grape's are the same root, and Prokupac is still the dominant variety.

appellations.name: Niš
appellations.grapes: Prokupac, Tamjanika, Smederevka
appellations.summary: Niš, Roman Naissus and birthplace of Constantine the Great, has vineyards on the surrounding hills; Matejevac's slopes above the city are its best-known district, with a cellar row and a tradition of Prokupac and Tamjanika going back centuries.

appellations.name: Vranje
appellations.grapes: Prokupac, Vranac, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Tamjanika
appellations.summary: Vranje, in the far south near North Macedonia, is a warm, hilly PGI where Aleksić and other wineries make Prokupac, Vranac and international reds. Aleksić, one of Serbia's most awarded wineries, produces about 450,000 litres a year.

appellations.name: Jagodina
appellations.summary: Jagodina lies on the Velika Morava in central Serbia; its PGI covers the hills of the Pomoravlje district. Like most of Serbia's 81 wine geographical indications, it is protected under the 2021 UK-Serbia trade agreement and corresponds to a district of the national zoning; few producers use the name on labels so far.

appellations.name: Jelica
appellations.summary: Jelica is a mountain near Čačak in western Serbia, with vineyards on its southern slopes. Like most of Serbia's 81 wine geographical indications, it is protected under the 2021 UK-Serbia trade agreement and corresponds to a district of the national zoning; few producers use the name on labels so far.

appellations.name: Jovac
appellations.summary: Jovac is a village near Vladičin Han in the Južna Morava valley in southern Serbia. Like most of Serbia's 81 wine geographical indications, it is protected under the 2021 UK-Serbia trade agreement and corresponds to a district of the national zoning; few producers use the name on labels so far.

appellations.name: Ljubić
appellations.summary: Ljubić is the hill district of Čačak in western Serbia, site of an 1815 battle of the Second Serbian Uprising. Like most of Serbia's 81 wine geographical indications, it is protected under the 2021 UK-Serbia trade agreement and corresponds to a district of the national zoning; few producers use the name on labels so far.

appellations.name: Džervin

appellations.name: Tiranë
appellations.summary: Tirana's district includes Shesh, which gave its name to the Shesh grapes, and the Kokomani winery at Ndroq. It is one of 36 Albanian wine names protected in the United Kingdom under the UK-Albania trade agreement, matching the historic district boundaries; few labels use it yet.

appellations.name: Tropojë
appellations.summary: Tropojë is the remote north-eastern mountain district of the Valbona valley. It is one of 36 Albanian wine names protected in the United Kingdom under the UK-Albania trade agreement, matching the historic district boundaries; few labels use it yet.

appellations.name: Vlorë
appellations.summary: Vlorë, on the bay where Albania's independence was declared in 1912, is home to the Vlosh red, grown around Narta. It is one of 36 Albanian wine names protected in the United Kingdom under the UK-Albania trade agreement, matching the historic district boundaries; few labels use it yet.

appellations.name: Cotnari
appellations.grapes: Grasă de Cotnari, Fetească Albă, Tămâioasă Românească, Frâncușă, Busuioacă de Bohotin
appellations.summary: Cotnari, in the hills north-west of Iași, is Romania's most famous historic wine and its answer to Tokaj. The DOC (nine communes) is dedicated to four local whites: Grasă de Cotnari, Fetească Albă, Tămâioasă Românească and Frâncușă, plus the pink Busuioacă de Bohotin. Autumn fogs bring noble rot to Grasă, the same grape as Tokaj's Kövérszőlő, and the best wines are sweet, honeyed and long-lived; residual sugar of about 300 g/l is common, and the 1958 harvest reached about 520 g/l. The vineyards are documented since the 15th century and reached their peak under Peter II, Stephen the Great (1457 to 1504) and Despot Vodă, who founded a Latin school at Cotnari in 1562. The large Cotnari company, privatised after 1989, is one of Romania's biggest single estates, and Casa de Vinuri Cotnari makes dry versions of the same grapes.
appellations.terroir: Clay and sandy loams on the Cotnari hills at 150 to 400 m; autumn fogs encourage botrytis; continental climate with harsh winters.
appellations.nerd_note: Cotnari's Grasă and Tokaj's Kövérszőlő are the same variety: two historic sweet-wine regions on either side of the Carpathians share a grape.

appellations.name: Dealu Mare
appellations.grapes: Fetească Neagră, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinot Noir, Syrah, Fetească Albă, Fetească Regală, Tămâioasă Românească
appellations.summary: Dealu Mare ('the big hill') is Romania's leading red-wine DOC: a 65 km band of south-facing foothills from Buzău to Ploiești, with 18 to 20 communes including Urlați, Ceptura, Valea Călugărească, Breaza, Merei and Năeni. Sheltered by the Carpathians and open to the southern sun, it ripens Fetească Neagră, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon and Pinot Noir into rich, plush reds, and its eastern end produces aromatic sweet Tămâioasă. It was where phylloxera first appeared in Romania, at Chitorani, and it is now the base of many of the country's best modern wineries: Davino, LacertA, Serve, Budureasca, Basilescu, Rotenberg, Aurelia Vișinescu, Crama Gîrboiu's neighbours and the historic Halewood estate. Sub-denominations such as Urlați, Valea Călugărească, Ceptura, Merei, Breaza, Zorești and Tohani can appear on labels.
appellations.terroir: South-facing slopes of 130 to 550 m on clays, marls and loess; warm and sunny, sheltered from northern cold.
appellations.nerd_note: Valea Călugărească ('valley of the monks') houses Romania's national viticulture research institute, which has bred and selected many of the country's clones.

appellations.name: Murfatlar
appellations.grapes: Chardonnay, Pinot Gris, Muscat Ottonel, Tămâioasă Românească, Fetească Neagră, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: Murfatlar lies just inland from Constanța on the Black Sea, in Dobrogea's chalky, sun-baked hills; it is one of the sunniest vineyard areas in Europe, with very little rain. The DOC (14 communes, with sub-denominations Medgidia, Cernavodă and Megidia) became famous under Communism for rich, late-harvested, often sweet Chardonnay, Pinot Gris and Muscat Ottonel from the big state winery and research station; today the Murfatlar company and smaller estates also make ripe reds from Fetească Neagră, Merlot and Cabernet. The local white crossing Columna was bred at the Murfatlar station.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and chalky loess plateaus; very warm and dry, over 300 days of sun, moderated by the Black Sea.

appellations.name: Târnave
appellations.grapes: Fetească Regală, Fetească Albă, Riesling Italian, Muscat Ottonel, Sauvignon Blanc, Traminer, Pinot Gris
appellations.summary: Târnave is the largest Transylvanian DOC, covering the valleys of the Târnava Mare and Târnava Mică between Blaj, Mediaș and Sighișoara (about 35 communes). It is cool and high, so the wines are crisp, aromatic whites: Fetească Regală (first noted at Daneș nearby), Fetească Albă, Riesling Italian, Muscat Ottonel, Sauvignon Blanc and Traminer, plus traditional-method sparkling. Jidvei, Romania's largest estate with about 2,500 ha, dominates; its headquarters is the Bethlen-Haller castle at Cetatea de Baltă. Sub-denominations include Jidvei, Mediaș, Blaj, Dealurile Mureșului and Dumbrăveni.
appellations.terroir: Marl and clay hills at 300 to 500 m; cool continental climate, late harvest, high acidity.

appellations.name: Drăgășani
appellations.grapes: Crâmpoșie Selecționată, Tămâioasă Românească, Sauvignon Blanc, Fetească Regală, Negru de Drăgășani, Novac, Fetească Neagră
appellations.summary: Drăgășani follows the right bank of the Olt in Vâlcea county, a long chain of hills with eleven communes. It is known for crisp, herbal Crâmpoșie Selecționată, aromatic Tămâioasă Românească, Sauvignon Blanc, and two reds bred here, Negru de Drăgășani and Novac. The Știrbey family estate, restituted in 2001 and revived by Ileana Kripp-Costinescu and the Austrian winemaker Oliver Bauer, made the area's modern reputation; Avincis and Bauer are other leading names.
appellations.nerd_note: Novac and Negru de Drăgășani were both bred at the Drăgășani research station in the 1980s and 1990s by crossing the local Negru Vârtos with Georgia's Saperavi.

appellations.name: Recaș
appellations.grapes: Fetească Neagră, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Pinot Noir, Syrah, Fetească Regală, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Recaș is a single-commune DOC near Timișoara built around Cramele Recaș, rebuilt from 1998 by Romanian and British partners into one of Romania's largest and most export-focused wineries, with about 1,000 ha. Its vineyards date from the 15th century. It makes everything from inexpensive varietals to the Solo Quinta and Cuvée Uberland ranges, and is the source of much of the Romanian wine seen in UK supermarkets.

appellations.name: Pietroasa
appellations.grapes: Tămâioasă Românească, Grasă de Cotnari, Busuioacă de Bohotin, Fetească Neagră
appellations.summary: Pietroasa, a single commune (Pietroasele) at the eastern end of the Dealu Mare hills in Buzău county, is famous for sweet Tămâioasă Românească grown on limestone-rich slopes; the University of Agronomic Sciences in Bucharest runs a research station here. The village is also where the Pietroasa Treasure, a 4th-century Gothic gold hoard, was found in 1837.

appellations.name: Odobești
appellations.grapes: Galbenă de Odobești, Fetească Albă, Fetească Regală, Riesling Italian, Băbească Neagră, Fetească Neagră
appellations.summary: Odobești, in Vrancea, is one of Romania's oldest and most extensive vineyard areas, on the slopes below the Măgura Odobești. It is known for whites, especially the tart local Galbenă de Odobești, Fetească Albă and Riesling Italian, and large-volume production.

appellations.name: Panciu
appellations.grapes: Fetească Albă, Fetească Regală, Riesling Italian, Muscat Ottonel, Șarba, Galbenă de Odobești, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Panciu, in northern Vrancea, is known for crisp whites and above all for sparkling wine: the DOC covers quality sparkling and aromatic sparkling (Muscat Ottonel, Tămâioasă, Șarba) as well as still wines, and the town's old cellars, rebuilt after the 1940 and 1977 earthquakes, hold millions of bottles. The area was a front line in World War I (Mărășești, 1917).

appellations.name: Cotești
appellations.grapes: Fetească Neagră, Băbească Neagră, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Fetească Albă, Riesling Italian
appellations.summary: Cotești, in southern Vrancea, makes both whites and the region's best-known reds (Fetească Neagră, Băbească Neagră, Merlot) on warmer south-facing slopes; it has high permitted yields and is largely a volume area.

appellations.name: Huși
appellations.grapes: Zghihară de Huși, Fetească Albă, Fetească Regală, Busuioacă de Bohotin, Aligoté, Fetească Neagră
appellations.summary: Huși, near the Prut and the Moldovan border, is famous for Zghihară de Huși, a tart, light local white, and for being a favourite source of wine for the Communist leadership. The DOC covers 17 communes with a long variety list.

appellations.name: Iași
appellations.grapes: Fetească Albă, Fetească Regală, Aligoté, Busuioacă de Bohotin, Golia, Arcaș, Fetească Neagră
appellations.summary: The Iași DOC surrounds Moldavia's historic capital, with 13 communes on hills such as Copou and Bucium. It makes aromatic whites and some reds, and is home to university research that bred the Golia and Arcaș varieties.

appellations.name: Bohotin
appellations.grapes: Busuioacă de Bohotin, Fetească Albă, Fetească Regală, Aligoté
appellations.summary: Bohotin, south-east of Iași near the Prut, gives its name to Busuioacă de Bohotin, a pink-skinned muscat with a basil-like perfume (*busuioc* means basil), made dry or sweet as a dark rosé. The DOC covers six communes.

appellations.name: Iana
appellations.grapes: Fetească Albă, Fetească Regală, Aligoté, Busuioacă de Bohotin, Băbească Neagră
appellations.summary: Iana is a small DOC in Vaslui county in central Moldavia (five communes), producing light whites and reds from Fetească Albă, Aligoté, Băbească Neagră and Busuioacă de Bohotin. Most of its wine is sold locally and in bulk; the DOC exists largely to protect a historic name.

appellations.name: Nicorești
appellations.grapes: Băbească Neagră, Fetească Neagră, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Fetească Albă
appellations.summary: Nicorești, in Galați county, is the classic home of Băbească Neagră, a light, sour-cherry red with bright acidity and low tannin that is best drunk young and cool. The DOC (eight communes) also produces Fetească Neagră and whites.

appellations.name: Dealu Bujorului
appellations.grapes: Băbească Neagră, Fetească Neagră, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Fetească Albă, Aligoté
appellations.summary: Dealu Bujorului ('peony hill') around Târgu Bujor in Galați county is a warm, southern Moldavian DOC with a research station; it makes reds (Băbească Neagră, Fetească Neagră, Merlot) and whites.

appellations.name: Sâmburești
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Pinot Noir, Fetească Neagră, Novac, Negru de Drăgășani
appellations.summary: Sâmburești, in Olt county, was a renowned Cabernet Sauvignon estate in the Communist era, when its reds were among Romania's most prestigious; the DOC covers two communes and is still known for Cabernet and Merlot.

appellations.name: Ștefănești
appellations.grapes: Fetească Regală, Fetească Albă, Riesling Italian, Tămâioasă Românească, Burgund Mare, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: Ștefănești, near Pitești in Argeș county, hosts a long-standing viticulture research station; the DOC (six communes) produces whites and reds from Fetească Regală, Riesling Italian, Tămâioasă and Burgund Mare (Blaufränkisch), with yields capped at 10 t/ha.

appellations.name: Banu Mărăcine
appellations.grapes: Fetească Neagră, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Novac, Tămâioasă Românească, Fetească Regală
appellations.summary: Banu Mărăcine is a small DOC around Craiova named after the University of Craiova's teaching and research station; it produces reds and whites from Fetească Neagră, Merlot, Cabernet and Tămâioasă.

appellations.name: Segarcea
appellations.grapes: Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinot Noir, Fetească Neagră, Merlot, Tămâioasă Roză, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay
appellations.summary: Segarcea, south of Craiova, was the Crown Domain (Domeniul Coroanei) of the Romanian royal family from 1884 until 1948; nationalised by the Communists, it was revived in the 2000s and now makes Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinot Noir, Fetească Neagră and Tămâioasă roză.

appellations.name: Mehedinți
appellations.grapes: Fetească Neagră, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah, Novac, Negru de Drăgășani, Tămâioasă Românească
appellations.summary: Mehedinți, in the far south-west near the Danube's Iron Gates and Drobeta-Turnu Severin, covers about 20 communes including the Corcova and Oprișor areas. Crama Oprișor and Corcova Roy & Dâmboviceanu make some of Romania's most structured reds here.

appellations.name: Alba Iulia
appellations.grapes: Fetească Albă, Fetească Regală, Riesling Italian, Muscat Ottonel, Traminer Roz, Neuburger, Pinot Gris
appellations.summary: Alba Iulia, around the citadel city on the Mureș where the union of Transylvania with Romania was proclaimed in 1918, is a small white-wine DOC of seven communes including Ighiu and Cricău. Riesling Italian, Fetească Regală, Muscat Ottonel and Traminer dominate.

appellations.name: Aiud
appellations.grapes: Fetească Regală, Fetească Albă, Riesling Italian, Muscat Ottonel, Traminer Roz, Iordana
appellations.summary: Aiud, north of Alba Iulia along the Mureș, makes crisp Transylvanian whites from Fetească Regală, Riesling Italian, Muscat Ottonel, Traminer and the local crossing Iordana. Its six communes include Ocna Mureș, a salt-mining town, and the hills are cool enough for good sparkling base wine.

appellations.name: Sebeș-Apold
appellations.grapes: Fetească Regală, Riesling Italian, Muscat Ottonel, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Gris, Pinot Noir, Iordana
appellations.summary: Sebeș-Apold spans the hills between Sebeș and the Saxon villages of Apold and Gârbova; its 12 communes make fresh whites and some reds, and the area's Saxon fortified churches recall its German past.

appellations.name: Lechința
appellations.grapes: Fetească Regală, Fetească Albă, Riesling Italian, Sauvignon Blanc, Traminer Roz, Pinot Noir
appellations.summary: Lechința, in Bistrița-Năsăud in northern Transylvania, is a cool white-wine DOC of 17 communes; Liliac's modern winery at Batoș has raised its profile with crisp Fetească Regală, Sauvignon and Pinot Noir.

appellations.name: Oltina
appellations.grapes: Fetească Neagră, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: Oltina lies in south-western Dobrogea near the Danube and the Bulgarian border, with seven communes including Aliman and Ostrov making ripe reds and whites in a warm, dry climate. The nearby Danube lakes temper the summer heat a little.

appellations.name: Adamclisi
appellations.grapes: Fetească Neagră, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc
appellations.summary: Adamclisi became Romania's newest DOC in July 2020, a single commune in southern Dobrogea named for the Roman Tropaeum Traiani monument. Its rules allow only six varieties (Fetească Neagră, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc) at a low 7 t/ha. Alira and Viile Metamorfosis' neighbours have planted modern vineyards here.

appellations.name: Babadag
appellations.grapes: Fetească Neagră, Băbească Neagră, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Aligoté, Fetească Regală, Columna
appellations.summary: Babadag, in northern Dobrogea near the Razim-Sinoe lagoons of the Danube Delta and the Greek ruins of Histria, covers 13 communes making whites and reds in a dry, windy climate. Aligoté and the Murfatlar-bred Columna are local specialities.

appellations.name: Sarica Niculițel
appellations.grapes: Aligoté, Fetească Neagră, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Fetească Regală, Rkatsiteli
appellations.summary: Sarica Niculițel, near Tulcea at the gateway to the Danube Delta, is a hilly DOC of 14 communes on the old Măcin hills, known for Aligoté, Fetească Neagră and Merlot.

appellations.name: Banat
appellations.grapes: Cadarcă, Burgund Mare, Fetească Neagră, Merlot, Riesling Italian, Fetească Regală, Majarcă Albă
appellations.summary: The Banat DOC covers the hills of Moldova Nouă and the Dealurile Tirolului near the Danube gorge and the Serbian border. It makes both reds and whites; the area's Czech-founded villages and Danube landscapes give it character.

appellations.name: Miniș
appellations.grapes: Cadarcă, Burgund Mare, Fetească Neagră, Mustoasă de Măderat, Fetească Regală, Riesling Italian, Furmint
appellations.summary: Miniș, in the Zărand hills near Arad, is one of Romania's oldest documented vineyard areas, famous for Cadarcă (Kadarka) red and the local white Mustoasă de Măderat; the DOC covers still, semi-sparkling and quality sparkling wine across nine communes.

appellations.name: Crișana
appellations.grapes: Fetească Regală, Fetească Albă, Riesling Italian, Mustoasă de Măderat, Pinot Gris, Fetească Neagră
appellations.summary: Crișana covers the north-western hills around Oradea, Diosig, Șimleu Silvaniei and Zalău (23 communes), close to the Hungarian border, making mostly whites from Fetească Regală, Riesling Italian and Mustoasă de Măderat, with some Fetească Neagră.

appellations.name: Însurăței
appellations.grapes: Fetească Albă, Fetească Regală, Riesling, Chardonnay, Fetească Neagră, Syrah, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: Însurăței, in Brăila county on the Danube plain, became a DOC in 2018 (four communes). It makes fresh whites and reds from Fetească Albă, Fetească Regală, Riesling, Chardonnay, Fetească Neagră, Syrah and Cabernet.

appellations.name: Melnik
appellations.grapes: Shiroka Melnishka Loza, Ranna Melnishka Loza (Melnik 55), Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
appellations.summary: The Melnik PDO covers the Petrich municipality around the tiny town of Melnik, Bulgaria's smallest with about 400 inhabitants, set among the sandstone and conglomerate 'earth pyramids' that rise up to 100 m above the Struma valley. Its grape is Shiroka Melnishka Loza (Broadleaf Melnik), a late-ripening red with small, dark berries that ripens in October and makes spicy, tobacco-scented, oak-loving wines; Melnik 55, its early-ripening offspring bred at Sandanski in 1963, is softer and riper. Melnik wine has been recorded since at least 1346, was shipped to Venice and beyond from merchants' rock-cut cellars such as the Kordopulov House (1754), and is said to have been Winston Churchill's favourite Bulgarian wine.
appellations.terroir: Sandy and sandstone soils at the foot of the Pirin; hot, dry sub-Mediterranean climate funnelled up the Struma valley.
appellations.nerd_note: Shiroka Melnishka Loza is a parent of Ranna Melnishka Loza (Melnik 55), whose other parent DNA testing identified as the French Valdiguié.

appellations.name: Dolinata na Struma
appellations.grapes: Shiroka Melnishka Loza, Melnik 55, Keratsuda, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Syrah
appellations.summary: Dolinata na Struma ('Struma Valley') is the broad PDO covering 22 municipalities along the Struma from Pernik and Kyustendil south to Petrich and Sandanski, including Blagoevgrad and Kresna. It frames all the south-west's wine styles, from Broadleaf Melnik and Melnik 55 to Cabernet, Merlot and the rare Keratsuda white of Kresna.

appellations.name: Sandanski
appellations.grapes: Melnik 55, Shiroka Melnishka Loza, Sandanski Misket, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
appellations.summary: Sandanski, at the foot of the Pirin in the Struma valley, is one of Bulgaria's warmest wine towns. Its research station bred Melnik 55 in 1963, and the local Sandanski Misket is a rare aromatic white. The PDO covers the Sandanski municipality.

appellations.name: Harsovo
appellations.grapes: Shiroka Melnishka Loza, Melnik 55, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
appellations.summary: Harsovo, a village in the Sandanski municipality near Melnik, gives its name to a small PDO in the heart of Broadleaf Melnik country. Villa Melnik's estate is nearby. Like the rest of the Struma valley it enjoys the warm air that funnels north from the Aegean.

appellations.name: Asenovgrad
appellations.grapes: Mavrud, Rubin, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
appellations.summary: Asenovgrad, at the edge of the Rhodopes south-east of Plovdiv, is the traditional heartland of Mavrud, the late-ripening, thick-skinned native red that makes dark, tannic wines with blackberry, mulberry and spice. The PDO covers Asenovgrad, Parvomai and Sadovo municipalities. Legend ties the grape's name to a young man of Khan Krum's time whose wine-fuelled courage saved the vineyards.
appellations.nerd_note: Mavrud vines are often trained low and need a long, warm autumn; the best old vines sit on the alluvial terraces of the Chaya river below the Rhodope foothills.

appellations.name: Perushtitsa
appellations.grapes: Mavrud, Rubin, Cabernet Sauvignon
appellations.summary: Perushtitsa, south-west of Plovdiv at the foot of the Rhodopes, is the second classic home of Mavrud; its PDO covers part of the Rodopi municipality. The town is also a national shrine for its role in the April Uprising of 1876.

appellations.name: Brestnik
appellations.grapes: Mavrud, Rubin, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
appellations.summary: Brestnik, a village in the Rodopi municipality just south of Plovdiv, has its own PDO for reds from Mavrud, Rubin, Cabernet and Merlot grown on the first Rhodope foothills. Its slopes rise just above the Maritsa plain, where the alluvial soils give way to the stonier ground that Mavrud prefers.
